 Follow Florida AMC movie theater in mall permanently closed amid renovations
 Valeria Bartra, Treasure Coast Newspapers Updated Mon, November 9, 2026 at 6:11 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. The Vero Beach movie theater in the mall closed permanently on Nov. 8.
 AMC Theatres decided to close the AMC Classic Indian River 24 "based on what will best strengthen the company going forward," according to AMC spokesperson Cassie Kennard.
 The website directs customers to AMC's theater in Melbourne and Kennard directed them to AMC Port St. Lucie 14 in St. Lucie West.
 The aging Indian River Mall at 6200 20th St., which opened in 1996 and declined after years of store closures, is being transformed from an indoor mall to mixed-use retail with new outdoor stores and a drive-through restaurant.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Demolition for renovations on the east side of the mall began in August. The west section, including the movie theater, was supposed to remain operational, according to Joseph Scarfone of One Investment Group in Pompano Beach. He has been working with the mall owners, DTS Properties II of Illinois.

(BRIAN MERCURI | SPECIAL TO TCPALM) The mall owners submitted demolition and renovation plans in May 2025, but little movement has occurred.
 The project includes construction of five 250,000-square-foot outdoor retail stores and a drive-through restaurant. Negotiations are underway with a "really good list" of national tenants to fill those stores, Scarfone said.
 Once the outside remodeling is completed, the company plans to give the inside a facelift.
 Advertisement Advertisement Of the four stores that anchored the mall — JCPenney, Dillard's, Sears and Burdines — only JCPenney and Dillard's remain. Macy's closed in 2020 after 24 years at the mall, and Sears closed in 2019 after 23 years. Both closures were parts of national movements to shutter stores.
